Evidence: [Rijksmonument 3716](https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/3716), [JCK Portugese Synagoge](https://jck.nl/locatie/portugese-synagoge), [RCE book "The Portuguese Synagogue in Amsterdam"](https://english.cultureelerfgoed.nl/binaries/cultureelerfgoed-en/documenten/publications/2013/01/01/the-portuguese-synagogue-in-amsterdam/Portuguese-synagogue_EN_LR_web.pdf). Caveats: the live summary is all candles and wallpaper. The arrival paragraph is the main addition.

qs04c1uh8vx5juadbuq9a6kf.name: Vlooienburg, the first Jewish island, and Spinoza's statue
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 2. **Vlooienburg, the first Jewish island, and Spinoza's statue** (Amstel 7 / Zwanenburgwal, round the Stopera; from about 1600) (E: "Vlooienburg under the Stopera, the plaque that took thirty years, and Spinoza", qs04c1uh8vx5juadbuq9a6kf; cluster alt: "Jonas Daniël Meijerplein and Vlooienburg...", fh0mc9q8q9xkj6yovtkgia65): a timber-yard island made around 1593 where the first Portuguese newcomers rented houses. Their first prayer rooms were here: Beth Jacob, on the first floor of a house called Antwerpen on the Houtgracht, about 1602, then Neve Shalom and Beth Israel. Spinoza, son of a Portuguese merchant, was born at its edge. Who: Sephardic Jews, later the poor Ashkenazim. Era: 1600 to 1943. Status: gone (under the Stopera; plaque, model and Spinoza statue of 2008). Evidence: [Spinozaweb: Vlooienburg](https://spinozaweb.org/locations/3), [4en5mei Vlooienburgmonument](https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/4633/amsterdam-vlooienburgmonument), [Kunstwacht Spinoza Monument](https://amsterdam.kunstwacht.nl/kunstwerken/bekijk/546), [Wikipedia (nl) Vlooienburg](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vlooienburg). Caveats: the founding date of Beth Jacob differs by source (1597 in older encyclopedias, about 1602 in Spinozaweb and recent scholarship). Use "around 1600".

py728mskln2x7j728twnd5pg.name: The Great Synagogue (Jewish Museum)
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 3. **The Great Synagogue (Jewish Museum)** (Nieuwe Amstelstraat 1; 1671) (E: "Jewish Museum (Joods Museum), four synagogues in one", py728mskln2x7j728twnd5pg): Jews from German lands and then Poland came after the Sephardim, poorer and in larger numbers. By 1674 there were about 5,000 Ashkenazim against 2,500 Sephardim. Their Great Synagogue of 1671 stands opposite the Esnoga, and three more were added as the community grew. Who: Ashkenazi Jews from Germany and Poland. Era: 1635 to 1800. Status: changed (now the Jewish Museum). Evidence: [Rijksmonument 265](https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/265), [JCK Joods Museum](https://jck.nl/locatie/joods-museum), [Wikipedia (nl) Grote Synagoge](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grote_Synagoge_(Amsterdam)), [Jewish Virtual Library (Amsterdam)](https://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/history-of-jews-in-amsterdam). Caveats: the separate Polish congregation (1660, forced to merge in 1673) can go in this text; its prayer house has no known site.

gy73jsn1kntbnvgiwh1djw2o.name: Merwedeplein, the refugees' square
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 5. **Merwedeplein, the refugees' square** (Merwedeplein 37; 1933 to 1942) (E: "Merwedeplein, the Frank family's square", gy73jsn1kntbnvgiwh1djw2o): the Franks came from Frankfurt in 1933 and lived here among other German refugees. A 1941 list counts 163 foreign Jews on this one square, and the Rivierenbuurt became the refugees' neighbourhood. Who: German and Austrian Jewish refugees. Era: 1933 to 1942. Status: open (no. 37 is now a refuge flat for persecuted writers). Evidence: [Joods Amsterdam: Merwedeplein](https://www.joodsamsterdam.nl/merwedeplein/), [4en5mei Anne Frank statue](https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/2680/amsterdam-anne-frank-2), [Anne Frank House: Otto goes to the Netherlands](https://www.annefrank.org/annes-wereld/en/anne-frank/1933-emigration-netherlands/otto-goes-netherlands). Caveats: Anne's and Margot's schools are already their own places (see Borderline). Say so in the text and don't list them.

iod6ugp3yos61fyy3gy0sdjf.name: Huis De Pinto
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 7. **Huis De Pinto** (Sint Antoniesbreestraat 69; bought 1651) (E: "Huis De Pinto, the house that stopped a motorway", iod6ugp3yos61fyy3gy0sdjf): the De Pinto family came from Lisbon by way of Antwerp and Rotterdam. Isaack de Pinto bought this house in 1651, and his son gave it its Italianate front. It is the grandest surviving trace of the Portuguese Jews' rise on the Breestraat. Who: Sephardic Jews. Era: 1600 to 1800. Status: changed (public library and reading room). Evidence: [Rijksmonument 5431](https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/5431), [Wikipedia (en) Huis de Pinto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huis_de_Pinto), [Huis De Pinto](https://huisdepinto.nl/). Caveats: no source says they "fled" in 1651. Keep it as Lisbon via Antwerp, with the New Christian background in general terms.

e95bjuggykyeq3819ysm1y8o.name: Uilenburgersjoel and the Jewish island of the poor
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 9. **Uilenburgersjoel and the Jewish island of the poor** (Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 91; 1766) (E: "Uilenburgersjoel, the synagogue behind the wall", e95bjuggykyeq3819ysm1y8o; cluster alt: "Uilenburg, the Jewish island...", ef47x04a03yndqqtiht5s5pl): poor Ashkenazi newcomers from Germany and Eastern Europe crowded onto Uilenburg. Their synagogue of 1766 is reached only through an alley, in a court the High German community owned. Who: Ashkenazi Jews. Era: 1700 to 1943. Status: open (events and a congregation). Evidence: [Rijksmonument 5798](https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/5798), [Stichting Uilenburgersjoel](https://www.uilenburgersjoel.nl/herinneringen-van-morgen/), [Wikipedia (nl) Uilenburger Synagoge](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uilenburger_Synagoge). Caveats: list one of the two, not both.

qgebug2xadhtttz8fvvzlgbl.name: The Russensjoel, Nieuwe Kerkstraat 149
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 10. **The Russensjoel, Nieuwe Kerkstraat 149** (1889) (E: "The Russensjoel and the old \"Jodenkerkstraat\" (Nieuwe Kerkstraat 149)", qgebug2xadhtttz8fvvzlgbl): Jews fleeing the Russian pogroms, some of whom stopped in Amsterdam on the way to America, opened their own prayer house here in 1889. Who: Eastern European Jews. Era: 1880 to 1914. Status: changed (house). Evidence: [Rijksmonument 2960](https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/2960), [Joods Amsterdam: Nieuwe Kerkstraat](https://www.joodsamsterdam.nl/nieuwe-kerkstraat/). Caveats: none; the live text already tells the arrival story.

hfisq9jg2z8hguxong5ppm4s.name: Waterlooplein, over the Houtgracht synagogues
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 13. **Waterlooplein, over the Houtgracht synagogues** (Waterlooplein; Houtgracht filled 1882) (E: "Waterlooplein market, from Jewish market to flea market", hfisq9jg2z8hguxong5ppm4s): under the square lies the Houtgracht, where the three Portuguese congregations merged as Talmud Tora in 1639. Spinoza was banned in their synagogue in 1656. In 1882 the canals were filled and the Jewish street traders of the Jodenbreestraat were moved onto the new square. Who: Sephardic, then Ashkenazi Jews. Era: 1600 to 1940. Status: changed (flea market). Evidence: [Joods Amsterdam: Waterlooplein](https://www.joodsamsterdam.nl/waterlooplein/), [Spinozaweb: Vlooienburg (Talmud Tora at the Houtgracht)](https://spinozaweb.org/locations/3), [Wikipedia (en) Houtgracht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houtgracht). Caveats: the 1639 synagogue's exact plot (Houtgracht 208, later Waterlooplein 33-39, demolished 1931) needs a check against a map before it is pinned. I found no plaque.

tb18ar3l6vpng68y1wjv1x8c.name: Amsterdam Museum, the orphanage that sheltered refugee children
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 16. **Amsterdam Museum, the orphanage that sheltered refugee children** (Kalverstraat 92; 1938 to 1940) (E: "Amsterdam Museum (the Burgerweeshuis, Kalverstraat)", tb18ar3l6vpng68y1wjv1x8c): Jewish children from Germany and Austria, brought out by Truus Wijsmuller and others, stayed in the city orphanage. On 14 May 1940, 74 of them left Amsterdam and sailed from IJmuiden on the last boat to England. Who: German and Austrian Jewish refugee children. Era: 1938 to 1940. Status: changed (museum, closed for renovation). Evidence: [Anne Frank House timeline: Jewish children taken to England at the last minute](https://www.annefrank.org/en/timeline/63/jewish-children-taken-to-england-at-the-last-minute/), [Britannica: Kindertransport](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Kindertransport), [kindertransport-17uhr13.de: the last Kindertransport](https://kindertransport-17uhr13.de/der-letzte-kindertransport/?lang=en). Caveats: the count is 74 for the ship, with 66 sometimes given for the orphanage group. Some children lived with foster families.

mhthdzsjj6sab85nkewzaobi.name: Beethovenstraat, a street of German refugees
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 18. **Beethovenstraat, a street of German refugees** (Beethovenstraat at the Corellistraat) (E: "Beethovenstraat raids and tram stop", mhthdzsjj6sab85nkewzaobi): many German Jewish refugees found flats in the new Beethovenstraat, and the raids of 1943 came for them here. A pavement plate and a 2025 threshold mark the tram stop. Who: German Jewish refugees. Era: 1933 to 1943. Status: open (memorials). Evidence: [4en5mei (4570)](https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/monumenten_zoeken/oorlogsmonument/4570), [Joods Amsterdam: Beethovenstraat](https://www.joodsamsterdam.nl/beethovenstraat/), [NOS](https://nos.nl/l/2514671). Caveats: the memorials are about the deportation. The arrival paragraph has to carry the 1930s.

sznqovapkl7ekg0jj1dd6x0m.name: Blasiussjoel
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 20. **Blasiussjoel** (Swammerdamstraat 70; about 1900s) (E: "Blasiussjoel, Swammerdamstraat 70", sznqovapkl7ekg0jj1dd6x0m): the synagogue of Jews who had fled the Russian pogroms and settled in the Weesperzijde streets. Who: Eastern European Jews. Era: 1890 to 1943, reopened after the war. Status: changed (homes). Evidence: [Joods Amsterdam: synagoge Swammerdamstraat](https://www.joodsamsterdam.nl/synagoge-swammerdamstraat/), [Reliwiki](https://www.reliwiki.nl/index.php/Amsterdam,_Swammerdamstraat_70_-_Synagoge), [AHV wiki](https://www.amsterdamhv.nl/wiki/swammerdamstraat-70.html). Caveats: find the founding year before the text is written (not in my notes).

baktmd71by5dx5i3uikjobb9.name: Lekstraat synagogue
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 21. **Lekstraat synagogue** (Lekstraat 61-63; 1937) (E: "Lekstraat synagogue", baktmd71by5dx5i3uikjobb9): the last synagogue built before the war, for a Rivierenbuurt whose Jewish population grew from 4,000 to 17,000 in ten years, partly with refugees from Germany. Who: Dutch Jews moving south and German refugees. Era: 1930s. Status: changed (now a liberal-traditional congregation and Jewish centre). Evidence: [Rijksmonument 526707](https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/526707), [Joods Amsterdam: synagoge Lekstraat](https://www.joodsamsterdam.nl/synagoge-lekstraat/), [Wikipedia (nl) Lekstraatsynagoge](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lekstraatsynagoge). Caveats: most of the growth was Amsterdam Jews leaving the old quarter. Don't credit it all to refugees.

nrgi6zgog3xjlyaryea20c1r.name: Liberal Jewish synagogue, Zuidelijke Wandelweg
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 25. **Liberal Jewish synagogue, Zuidelijke Wandelweg** (2010; congregation 1932) (E: "The Liberal Jewish synagogue on Jacob Soetendorp's island", nrgi6zgog3xjlyaryea20c1r): Amsterdam's liberal congregation began in 1932, and between 1933 and 1940 its new members were mostly recent German Jewish immigrants, who brought the Reform tradition with them. The 2010 building is its fourth home. Who: German Jewish refugees. Era: 1932 to now. Status: open. Evidence: [Wikipedia (nl) Liberaal Joodse Gemeente Amsterdam](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberaal_Joodse_Gemeente_Amsterdam), [Joods Monument: Liberaal Joodse Gemeente](https://www.joodsmonument.nl/en/page/533/liberaal-joodse-gemeente), [Wikipedia (en) NVPJ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nederlands_Verbond_voor_Progressief_Jodendom). Caveats: the prewar meeting place is unknown (see Borderline, Tolstraat). The building itself is postwar, so the link is the community, not the site.

v2afj88x7n1qyna20hab9rwv.name: Huize Avondrood
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 26. **Huize Avondrood** (Nieuwe Herengracht 143; 1720) (E: "Huize Avondrood, a merchant's house with nine lives (Nieuwe Herengracht 143)", v2afj88x7n1qyna20hab9rwv): built for a Sephardic merchant, it later sheltered exiles from the Boer War. Two arrival stories in one house. Who: Sephardic Jews; Boer exiles. Era: 1720 to 1902. Status: changed (homes, squatted 1980). Evidence: [Rijksmonument 1943](https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/1943), [Wikipedia (nl) Nieuwe Herengracht 143](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nieuwe_Herengracht_143). Caveats: the Sephardic merchant was established here, not a newcomer. A weaker arrival hook; the Boer exiles also fit the 1800-1945 slice.

o0mpgfjnaymw9nhjzjwfpbcm.name: Jewish cemetery Zeeburg
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 27. **Jewish cemetery Zeeburg** (Valentijnkade, Flevopark; 1714 to 1942) (E: "Jewish cemetery Zeeburg", o0mpgfjnaymw9nhjzjwfpbcm): the burial ground of the poor Ashkenazi majority, about 100,000 people, most of them children. It is the only Ashkenazi cemetery inside the city. Who: Ashkenazi Jews. Era: 1714 to 1942. Status: open on Sunday afternoons in season. Evidence: [Monumentenregister Amsterdam](https://data.amsterdam.nl/monumenten/9e0da8a0-10e1-4e97-8edc-ee83c9e43790), [Stichting Eerherstel Zeeburg](https://www.eerherstelzeeburg.nl/index.html), [Joods Amsterdam: begraafplaats Zeeburg](https://www.joodsamsterdam.nl/begraafplaats-zeeburg/). Caveats: a "where they ended" place rather than an arrival place. Include only if the map wants one cemetery.

v4dfz50jf57ixhkh46pcjnp6.name: Twelve stumbling stones at Nieuwe Prinsengracht 18
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 28. **Twelve stumbling stones at Nieuwe Prinsengracht 18** (E: "Twelve stumbling stones at one door (Nieuwe Prinsengracht 18)", v4dfz50jf57ixhkh46pcjnp6): twelve stones at one door, many for refugees from Germany and Poland who had found rooms in one house. Who: German and Polish Jewish refugees. Era: 1933 to 1943. Status: open (stones). Evidence: [Buurtorganisatie 1018: struikelstenen](https://www.buurtorganisatie1018.nl/struikelstenen-in-1018), [Wikipedia (nl) Stolpersteine Centrum](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lijst_van_Stolpersteine_in_Amsterdam-Centrum). Caveats: lower priority. It duplicates the Beethovenstraat story in a different district.

c0l0ko0pn1um38r9zrmkeijw.name: Michelangelostraat 36, the Hidden Camera
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 30. **Michelangelostraat 36, the Hidden Camera** (1944 to 1945) (E: "Michelangelostraat 36, hideout of the Hidden Camera", c0l0ko0pn1um38r9zrmkeijw): the German Jewish filmmaker Fritz Kahlenberg, in hiding in this attic, ran the photographers of the Ondergedoken Camera with Tonny van Renterghem. Who: German Jewish refugee. Era: 1940 to 1945. Status: changed (house). Evidence: [NIOD: De Ondergedoken Camera](https://www.niod.nl/en/projects/underground-camera), [UNESCO NL Memory of the World](https://www.unesco.nl/nl/nl-memory-world-register/de-ondergedoken-camera). Caveats: when and why Kahlenberg came to the Netherlands is not confirmed in my sources. Verify before saying "refugee".

negoeq5xe2uuuvdqy81q3695.name: Centraal Station, the cold welcome plaque
lines: [jewish-arrivals] 31. **Centraal Station, the cold welcome plaque** (Oosttunnel, IJ side; 1945) (E: "Centraal Station's two plaques: the cold welcome and the sergeant", negoeq5xe2uuuvdqy81q3695): the plaque states that the government failed the camp survivors it received here in 1945. It marks the second arrival, the return. Who: Jewish survivors returning. Era: 1945. Status: open (plaque). Evidence: [4en5mei Herinnering (4962)](https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/4962/amsterdam-herinnering). Caveats: one authoritative source only so far. Add a news report of the 2019 unveiling before using it.

rnukdpl6s0wlpxykmtk08d2q.name: National Slavery Monument and Keti Koti
lines: [postwar-colonial] 1. **National Slavery Monument and Keti Koti** (Oosterpark, south-west corner; 2002) (E: "National Slavery Monument and Keti Koti", rnukdpl6s0wlpxykmtk08d2q): the national monument to the abolition of 1863 and, every 1 July, the place where Surinamese and Antillean Amsterdammers lead the Keti Koti commemoration; at the 2002 unveiling descendants were kept outside the fences. Who: Afro-Surinamese and Afro-Caribbean Amsterdammers. Era: 2002 to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; [Ons Amsterdam, Oosterpark 1 juli 2002](https://onsamsterdam.nl/artikelen/oosterpark-1-juli-2002-onthulling-slavernijmonument); [Koninklijke Verzamelingen, moments of the monument](https://www.koninklijkeverzamelingen.nl/verhalen/belangrijke-momenten-van-het-nationaal-monument-slavernijverleden). Caveats: existing text is strong; a short arrival paragraph only (who carries the day, why Amsterdam).

bltlk8q7ofxahychj8fo1vh8.name: Gliphoeve, the Bijlmer flats Surinamese activists squatted
lines: [postwar-colonial] 2. **Gliphoeve, the Bijlmer flats Surinamese activists squatted** (Geldershoofd and Gravestein; 1974 to 1975) (E: "Gliphoeve, the Bijlmer flats Surinamese activists squatted", bltlk8q7ofxahychj8fo1vh8): when housing quotas kept Surinamese out of whole neighbourhoods and families were stuck in pensions, activists squatted empty honeycomb flats in 1974; by the mid-1970s about 2,100 people lived in Gliphoeve I, nearly 90% Surinamese, and the Bijlmer became the arrival district of the 1975 wave. Who: Surinamese. Era: 1974 to now. Status: changed (Gliphoeve I demolished; Gliphoeve II renamed Geldershoofd). Evidence: [Stadsarchief, 1975 Uittocht na Surinaamse onafhankelijkheid](https://www.amsterdam.nl/stadsarchief/themasites/amsterdam-migratiestad/1975-uittocht-surinaamse/); [AT5, Na 1975 werd de Bijlmer het nieuwe thuis voor Surinamers](https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/235661/na-1975-werd-de-bijlmer-het-nieuwe-thuis-voor-surinamers-we-hebben-het-zelf-gedaan); [Volkskrant, Hoe de Bijlmer de Bijlmer werd](https://www.volkskrant.nl/nieuws-achtergrond/hoe-de-bijlmer-de-bijlmer-werd-het-verhaal-van-de-voormalige-gliphoeve-bewoners~bff251d4/). Caveats: the "Bijlmermeer" place (et0awp08hhog3xeyhfwv3crm) could carry the general 1975 arrival paragraph instead; pick one as the anchor.

nk0m8e7ajdmdq0vht0rpaivf.name: Javakade arrival tiles
lines: [postwar-colonial] 4. **Javakade arrival tiles** (Javakade, Java-eiland; ships of April and May 1951, tiles May 2026) (N; could also hang on E "Zeeman op de uitkijk and the head of the Java-eiland", nk0m8e7ajdmdq0vht0rpaivf): four ships (New Australia, Groote Beer, Somersetshire, Asturias) brought Moluccan ex-KNIL soldiers and their families to this quay by the Stoomvaart Maatschappij Nederland office; in May 2026 four memorial tiles with the ships and arrival dates, designed by Lars Bogaers (SNARS), were set in the pavement. Who: Moluccans. Era: 1951. Status: open (tiles; a permanent monument is planned inside the future Slavernijmuseum). Evidence: [Gemeente Amsterdam, 75 jaar Molukkers (Gedenktegels)](https://www.amsterdam.nl/sociaaldomein/diversiteit/75-jaar-molukkers/); [Amsterdam Museum, Javakade: Aankomst in Amsterdam](https://www.amsterdammuseum.nl/verhalen-en-collecties/themes/samangat-moluks-in-amsterdam/javakade). Caveats: the Amsterdam Museum page totals "about 4,600" but its ship figures add to roughly 4,100; quote per ship, not the total. Exact tile spot to confirm on site.

xfz0lp41wyazu32abhv8il7y.name: Beta berlayar jauh, the Moluccan marines' monument
lines: [postwar-colonial] 5. **Beta berlayar jauh, the Moluccan marines' monument** (Marineterrein, Kattenburgerstraat 5; 2026) (E: "Beta berlayar jauh, the Moluccan marines' monument", xfz0lp41wyazu32abhv8il7y): unveiled on 29 April 2026, 75 years after the first ship, for the Moluccan marines stationed at the Kattenburg barracks in 1951; the soldiers were discharged soon after arrival and their families sent to camps. Who: Moluccans. Era: 1951 to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; [Gemeente Amsterdam, 75 jaar Molukkers](https://www.amsterdam.nl/sociaaldomein/diversiteit/75-jaar-molukkers/); [Amsterdam Museum, Ton Louhenapessy en Marine Molukkers](https://www.amsterdammuseum.nl/verhalen-en-collecties/themes/samangat-moluks-in-amsterdam/ton-louhenapessy). Caveats: existing text already has the arrival story.

pui8gmz7znjzym8jscmd8zgo.name: Hotel Jakarta, on the old Indies passenger quay
lines: [postwar-colonial] 6. **Hotel Jakarta, on the old Indies passenger quay** (Javakade 766; quay used to 1960s, hotel 2018) (E: "Hotel Jakarta", pui8gmz7znjzym8jscmd8zgo): the tip of the Java-eiland is where the SMN liners left for and returned from the Indies, so repatriates and the 1951 Moluccans landed alongside; the Kop van Java is now the chosen site for the Nationaal Slavernijmuseum (opening delayed to 2033), which already runs a small Moluccan presentation in the hotel. Who: Indische repatriates, Moluccans; slavery remembrance. Era: 1946 to now. Status: changed (now hotel). Evidence: [Amsterdam750, Java-eiland en Hotel Jakarta](https://amsterdam750.nl/verhaal/van-golfbreker-tot-ontmoetingsplek-het-verhaal-van-java-eiland-en-hotel-jakarta/); [Gemeente Amsterdam, Nationaal Slavernijmuseum](https://www.amsterdam.nl/nationaal-slavernijmuseum/); [Parool, opening delayed to 2033](https://www.parool.nl/amsterdam/opening-nationaal-slavernijmuseum-vertraagd-tot-2033-gemeente-zoekt-naar-tijdelijke-locatie~b46513e8/). Caveats: existing text is about the garden; needs the arrival paragraph. Don't double-count with no. 4: tiles = Moluccans, hotel = the quay and the museum to come.

gpqpa6wg4twhxhjy8fsvaq77.name: Anton de Kom monument
lines: [postwar-colonial] 7. **Anton de Kom monument** (Anton de Komplein; 2006) (E: "Anton de Kom monument", gpqpa6wg4twhxhjy8fsvaq77): the Surinamese writer of Wij slaven van Suriname, honoured in the heart of Surinamese Amsterdam; at the 2006 unveiling opponents covered it with the Surinamese flag, and the debate about how he is shown still runs. Who: Surinamese. Era: 2006 to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; [4 en 5 mei, monument voor Anton de Kom](https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/939/amsterdam-monument-voor-anton-de-kom); [NPO Blend, de langlopende strijd om Anton de Kom](https://www.npoblend.nl/nieuws/een-waardig-beeld-de-langlopende-strijd-om-anton-de-kom). Caveats: pair with Reestraat 6 (1800-1945 slice) for the before/after.

mznh96x29f5wuldgqmlm6qqy.name: Levensboom, Monument van Besef
lines: [postwar-colonial] 8. **Levensboom, Monument van Besef** (Surinameplein; 2003) (E: "Levensboom, Monument van Besef", mznh96x29f5wuldgqmlm6qqy): the community's own slavery memorial, where Surinamese Amsterdammers have marked the night before Keti Koti on 30 June since 1993. Who: Afro-Surinamese. Era: 1993 to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; Stadscuratorium entry for the Levensboom (to add); [Koninklijke Verzamelingen](https://www.koninklijkeverzamelingen.nl/verhalen/belangrijke-momenten-van-het-nationaal-monument-slavernijverleden). Caveats: need one more authoritative link at write time.

ixmzhd415cly8a0avk7utsdo.name: Nelson Mandelapark and Kwaku
lines: [postwar-colonial] 9. **Nelson Mandelapark and Kwaku** (Nelson Mandelapark; 1975 to 2026) (E: "Nelson Mandelapark and Kwaku", ixmzhd415cly8a0avk7utsdo): Kwaku began in 1975, the year of independence, as a football tournament for Surinamese kids who could not afford a holiday and became the summer festival of Surinamese Amsterdam; 2026 was its last edition in this form. Who: Surinamese, later all diasporas of Zuidoost. Era: 1975 to now. Status: changed. Evidence: existing text; Kwaku coverage in Parool/AT5 (add at write time). Caveats: existing text already strong.

ztxusocyqxritry12i9dtpgw.name: Cotton Club, the Nieuwmarkt's Surinamese jazz café
lines: [postwar-colonial] 10. **Cotton Club, the Nieuwmarkt's Surinamese jazz café** (Nieuwmarkt 5; postwar) (E: "Cotton Club, the Nieuwmarkt's Surinamese jazz café", ztxusocyqxritry12i9dtpgw): the first haunt of the small postwar Surinamese community and of Black American soldiers, named after the Surinamese trumpeter Teddy Cotton. Who: Surinamese. Era: late 1940s onward. Status: open (café). Evidence: existing text; [Stadsarchief, Jazz-jaren](https://www.amsterdam.nl/stadsarchief/agenda/jazz-jaren-1/) (for Cotton's 1930s presence). Caveats: the cluster "Around the Nieuwmarkt, migrant Amsterdam" (q1ogooimbt808nocosyfc1nu) duplicates; list single places, not both.

qv461jmu4hj8ffcmy2hvlscm.name: Toko Dun Yong
lines: [postwar-colonial] 15. **Toko Dun Yong** (Stormsteeg 9; 1950s) (E: "Toko Dun Yong, the Chinese shop that grew out of a button shop", qv461jmu4hj8ffcmy2hvlscm): a former ship's stoker from Guangdong and his Rotterdam wife started the city's oldest Chinese toko by the Zeedijk; it grew into a five-storey store as Chinatown moved here from the Binnen Bantammerstraat. Who: Chinese. Era: 1950s to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; [Parool, De oudste toko vertelt de geschiedenis van Chinezen in Amsterdam](https://www.parool.nl/ps/de-oudste-toko-vertelt-de-geschiedenis-van-chinezen-in-amsterdam~b762242e/). Caveats: our text says 1957, Parool says 1959; check Karina Meeuwse's book.

gpfwuczovwew9d6b0r03exxw.name: He Hua temple
lines: [postwar-colonial] 16. **He Hua temple** (Zeedijk 106-118; 2000) (E: "He Hua temple, a Chinese palace on the Zeedijk", gpfwuczovwew9d6b0r03exxw): the Fo Guang Shan temple that the Chinese community built on a Zeedijk gap in the heroin years, opened by Queen Beatrix in 2000. Who: Chinese (Hong Kong, mainland, Chinese-Indonesian and Surinamese-Chinese Buddhists). Era: 2000 to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; [Ons Amsterdam, Honderd jaar Chinezen in Amsterdam](https://onsamsterdam.nl/artikelen/honderd-jaar-chinezen-in-amsterdam); [nl.wikipedia, Chinatown (Amsterdam)](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinatown_(Amsterdam)). Caveats: the community-mix claim to verify before writing.

fanacxlqejz0bxaddp3u4gwj.name: Taibah Mosque
lines: [postwar-colonial] 17. **Taibah Mosque** (Kraaiennest 125; 1980s) (E: "Taibah Mosque", fanacxlqejz0bxaddp3u4gwj): the mosque of Surinamese Hindustani Muslims who came with the 1970s wave, the "white pearl of the Bijlmer". Who: Surinamese Hindustani Muslims. Era: 1980s to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; Taibah's own history page and Parool coverage (add at write time). Caveats: founding and building dates to verify.

ie4fol049jb075kxpk62chkb.name: Wi Eegi Kerki
lines: [postwar-colonial] 19. **Wi Eegi Kerki** (Krommehoekstraat 136; 2013) (E: "Wi Eegi Kerki", ie4fol049jb075kxpk62chkb): "Our Own Church" in Sranan, the Moravian church of Surinamese Bijlmer residents, paid for by members after decades in borrowed halls; the Moravians (Evangelische Broedergemeente) are Suriname's largest Protestant church. Who: Afro-Surinamese Moravians. Era: 2013 to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; [Arcam, Wi Eegi Kerki](https://arcam.nl/architectuur-gids/wi-eegi-kerki/); [Gebouwd in Amsterdam](https://gebouwdin.amsterdam.nl/projectdetail/1108). Caveats: existing text is architectural; needs the community paragraph.

u8rcqo3ac70pzxf651zhfs2z.name: Koningskerk
lines: [postwar-colonial] 20. **Koningskerk** (Van 't Hofflaan 18-20, Watergraafsmeer; EBG since 1994) (E: "Koningskerk", u8rcqo3ac70pzxf651zhfs2z): since 1994 the city congregation of the Evangelische Broedergemeente worships here, many of them Surinamese; Trouw reported in 1995 that the congregation had led a wandering existence before. Who: Afro-Surinamese Moravians. Era: 1994 to now. Status: open. Evidence: [nl.wikipedia, Koningskerk (Amsterdam)](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koningskerk_(Amsterdam)); [Geheugen van Oost, Welkom in de Koningskerk](https://geheugenvanoost.amsterdam/page/104215/welkom-in-de-koningskerk-van-de-evangelische-broedergemeente-amsterdam); [Trouw 1995](https://www.trouw.nl/voorpagina/multi-functioneel-kerkcentrum-lenigt-ruimtenood-evangelische-broedergemeente-amsterdam~bb4de1bc/). Caveats: weaker twin of no. 19; take one if space is short.

xa9i2cwedrxrzwe9plns4ozd.name: Vogelparade
lines: [postwar-colonial] 21. **Vogelparade** (Hoogoorddreef at the Boy Edgarbrug; artwork) (E: "Vogelparade", xa9i2cwedrxrzwe9plns4ozd): eighteen empty birdcages salute the Surinamese songbird men of the Bijlmer and their twatwa contests, a custom brought from Paramaribo. Who: Surinamese. Era: 1970s to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; add a Parool/AT5 link on the twatwa contests at write time. Caveats: artwork, so the custom carries the item.

j1dd3utagdycmgtsoh00zdoi.name: Iron Lady of the Bijlmer
lines: [postwar-colonial] 22. **Iron Lady of the Bijlmer** (Brasapark; 2020s) (E: "Iron Lady of the Bijlmer", j1dd3utagdycmgtsoh00zdoi): portrait of Hilly Axwijk, who fought for Surinamese women in the G-buurt until 2004. Who: Surinamese women. Era: 1970s to 2004. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; add a stadsdeel or Parool link. Caveats: fine as is.

xwtk351ud1xm07u972oreg2z.name: Steven van Dorpel memorial
lines: [postwar-colonial] 24. **Steven van Dorpel memorial** (Nelson Mandelapark; 1989) (E: "Steven van Dorpel memorial", xwtk351ud1xm07u972oreg2z): the Bijlmer footballer killed in the 1989 Surinam Airways crash with most of the Kleurrijk Elftal, Dutch-Surinamese players flying home to play; the diaspora's grief, remembered in Zuidoost. Who: Surinamese. Era: 1989. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; nl.wikipedia, SLM-vlucht 764 (add). Caveats: fine.

w2ym89og3or6sdq4eu5thz9t.name: National Monument on the Dam: the empty urns and the Indies remembrance
lines: [postwar-colonial] 25. **National Monument on the Dam: the empty urns and the Indies remembrance** (Dam) (E: "National Monument on the Dam", w2ym89og3or6sdq4eu5thz9t): the two niches for Suriname and the Antilles never got their soil; and on 15 August the Indies commemoration of the end of the war in Asia is held here. Who: Surinamese, Antilleans, Indische Nederlanders. Era: 1956 to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; [NH Nieuws, Indië-herdenking op de Dam](https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/307365/indie-herdenking-op-de-dam-men-deed-alsof-die-oorlog-niet-meetelde-dat-was-pijnlijk); [NOS on the 2023 Dam commemoration](https://nos.nl/l/2485877). Caveats: A-list place; the 2023 speaker row is politics: mention the commemoration, not the quarrel.

pfjn559otru6beck3n9vn2xg.name: Monument Indië-Nederland
lines: [postwar-colonial] 26. **Monument Indië-Nederland** (Olympiaplein; 1935, renamed 2004) (E: "Monument Indië-Nederland (the former Van Heutsz monument)", pfjn559otru6beck3n9vn2xg): the old colonial general's monument rededicated to the shared history of the Netherlands and Indonesia, now the site of a decolonial Indonesia-Netherlands commemoration each August. Who: Indische Nederlanders, Indonesians, Moluccans. Era: 2004 to now. Status: open. Evidence: existing text; [NOS 2023](https://nos.nl/l/2485877); [Stadscuratorium, Monument Indië-Nederland](https://stadscuratorium.nl/collectie/monument-indie-nederland/). Caveats: politically charged; keep to facts (renaming, who gathers there).

qpw36rfj4uiq2fqhzjq0998g.name: De Bazel: NiNsee and the Kewang exhibition
lines: [postwar-colonial] 28. **De Bazel: NiNsee and the Kewang exhibition** (Vijzelstraat 32; NHM 1926, Stadsarchief 2007) (E: "De Bazel, the trading company's striped fortress, now the city archives", qpw36rfj4uiq2fqhzjq0998g): the head office of the Nederlandsche Handel-Maatschappij, the company that recruited the first Javanese contract workers for Suriname in 1890, now houses the Stadsarchief and NiNsee, the national institute for slavery history and its legacy (founded 2002); in 2026 its treasury showed "Claim Your Space: Kewang" with the Moluccan magazine Marinjo. Who: slavery remembrance; Javanese-Surinamese; Moluccans. Era: 2002 to now. Status: open. Evidence: [NiNsee contact (Vijzelstraat 32)](https://ninsee.nl/contact/); [Gemeente Amsterdam, 75 jaar Molukkers (Kewang)](https://www.amsterdam.nl/sociaaldomein/diversiteit/75-jaar-molukkers/); [Historiek, De Bazel koloniale geschiedenis](https://historiek.net/koloniale-geschiedenis-de-bazel/186002/). Caveats: NHM recruitment of the 1890 Javanese is from a Suriname Museum post: verify with an authoritative source. A teaching site reported NiNsee there "until September": check it hasn't moved.

yvotvixnz1htulngzttmr0ph.name: Centrumeiland's anti-colonial street names
lines: [postwar-colonial] 31. **Centrumeiland's anti-colonial street names** (Srefidensiplein and around, IJburg; named 2019) (N; Srefidensiplein has E "CPO Srefi Bow", yvotvixnz1htulngzttmr0ph, as a building only): 27 streets named after people from Suriname, the Antilles, Aruba and Indonesia who resisted colonialism and slavery, among them Otto and Hermina Huiswoud, Max Woiski Sr. and Jr., Virginia Dementricia of Aruba and Diponegoro; announced by the mayor at Keti Koti after KITLV research and NiNsee advice. Who: Surinamese, Antillean, Aruban, Indonesian heroes. Era: 2019. Status: open. Evidence: [Gemeenteblad 2019-173244](https://zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/gmb-2019-173244.pdf); [AT5, Wie zijn de verzetshelden achter de straatnamen](https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/196074/wie-zijn-de-verzetshelden-achter-de-straatnamen-van-het-nieuwe-centrumeiland); [Werkgroep Caraïbische Letteren](https://werkgroepcaraibischeletteren.nl/27-straten-vernoemd-naar-strijders-tegen-koloniale-overheersing/). Caveats: a "remembered" item, not a place newcomers used; borderline-strong.

mwfaf5jchs4htezhpu4y09ue.name: Albert Cuyp market, where Surinamese Amsterdam shopped
lines: [postwar-colonial] 32. **Albert Cuyp market, where Surinamese Amsterdam shopped** (Albert Cuypstraat) (E: "Albert Cuyp market", mwfaf5jchs4htezhpu4y09ue): after 1975 the market and its tokos were where you found Surinamese produce; Tjin's, a Surinamese-Chinese family shop, has been on the corner since 1981. Who: Surinamese, Surinamese-Chinese. Era: 1970s to now. Status: open. Evidence: [Geheugen van Oost, Surinaams koken in Nederland](https://geheugenvanoost.amsterdam/page/10192/surinaams-koken-in-nederland); [Flevolands Geheugen, Gezelligheid in De Pijp](https://www.flevolandsgeheugen.nl/page/5299/gezelligheid-in-de-pijp); [Tjin's Toko, about (official)](https://www.tjinstoko.com/pages/about). Caveats: memory sites plus a shop page: medium; an AT5 video exists on the same theme. Extra paragraph only.

v7j8193dfwx0l45gdhesooqa.name: Theosophical temple on the Tolstraat (Cinétol)
lines: [coordinator] Liberal Jewish synagogue 1937-1942 for a congregation grown with refugees from Germany (Otto Frank involved); a Moroccan mosque 1980-1982. The live text already tells both; set fields, extra_description short or none.

1800-1945.name: Querido Verlag, the exile publisher
1800-1945.line: 6. **Querido Verlag, the exile publisher** (Keizersgracht 333; 1933-1940) (N): after the Berlin book burning of May 1933 Emanuel Querido set up a German-language house run by Fritz Landshoff, ex-Kiepenheuer; it printed 124 books by banned writers (Heinrich Mann, Feuchtwanger, Döblin, Joseph Roth, Toller) and Klaus Mann's anti-Nazi monthly Die Sammlung. Dissolved May 1940; Querido was murdered in Sobibor in 1943. Who: German exile writers. Era: 1933-1940. Status: changed (canal house; no plaque found). Evidence: [Stadsarchief, Exil literatuur](https://www.amsterdam.nl/stadsarchief/stukken/tweede-wereldoorlog/exil-literatuur/); [Deutsche Nationalbibliothek, Querido Verlag 1933-1940](https://mediengeschichte.dnb.de/KIE/Content/EN/Topics/querido-en.html); Landshoff's memoir title "Amsterdam, Keizersgracht 333. Querido Verlag" ([bibliotheek.nl](https://www.bibliotheek.nl/catalogus/titel.066003490.html/fritz-h--landshoff)). Caveats: Keizersgracht 333 is the parent firm's seat (shared with Van Holkema & Warendorf); a check in the Stadsarchief address books would nail the Verlag's own rooms. A Parool piece says Querido got a stumbling stone: worth finding which address.

1800-1945.name: Castrum Peregrini
1800-1945.line: 17. **Castrum Peregrini** (Herengracht 401; 1942-1945) (N): the German poet and anti-Nazi exile Wolfgang Frommel lived from 1942 with the artist Gisèle van Waterschoot van der Gracht in her flat, where Jewish youths hid; it became a publishing house and foundation (now H401). Who: German exile, German-Jewish refugees in hiding. Era: 1940-1945. Status: open (H401 cultural centre). Evidence: [H401, Dealing with a complex past](https://h401.org/2018/10/dealing-with-a-complex-past/11103/); [Stadsarchief, Exil literatuur (Castrum Peregrini as clandestine press)](https://www.amsterdam.nl/stadsarchief/stukken/tweede-wereldoorlog/exil-literatuur/); [Kenan Malik, In the fortress of the pilgrims](https://kenanmalik.com/2016/05/08/in-the-fortress-of-the-pilgrims/). Caveats: the later abuse revelations around Frommel's circle are well documented; any text must mention them soberly or the place should go to Borderline.

1800-1945.name: Winkel van Sinkel
1800-1945.line: 23. **Winkel van Sinkel** (Nieuwendijk 174-176; 1822-1903) (N, gone): Anton Sinkel, born 1785 in Cloppenburg, opened his drapery here in 1822, the start of the store whose name became the Dutch byword for a shop that sells everything; young Krasnapolsky worked here. Who: German (Oldenburg). Era: 1822-1903. Status: gone (building demolished 1903; site later HEMA per Wikipedia). Evidence: [Rijksmuseum, drawing of the Winkel van Sinkel on the Nieuwendijk](https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en/collection/object/Gezicht-op-de-Winkel-van-Sinkel-op-de-Nieuwendijk--c5f20132ead2f8aa2bdedb8d387e466f); [Wikipedia, Winkel van Sinkel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winkel_van_Sinkel); [nl.wikipedia, A.W. Krasnapolsky](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolph_Wilhelm_Krasnapolsky). Caveats: opening year 1820/1821/1822 and house numbers vary; the famous building is the Utrecht branch. Better as one "German shopkeepers of the Nieuwendijk" cluster with P&C and C&A.

early-modern.name: Rey and Bernard's bookshop, the Huguenot publishers of Rousseau
early-modern.line: 18. **Rey and Bernard's bookshop, the Huguenot publishers of Rousseau** (Pijpenmarkt, now Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 296; mid-18th century) (N): Marc-Michel Rey, son of Huguenots from the Dauphiné who had fled to Geneva, and his wife Elisabeth Bernard, daughter of the Huguenot writer-publisher Jean Frédéric Bernard, ran the bookshop that printed Rousseau and smuggled the French Enlightenment past censorship; Rousseau became godfather to their daughter in 1762. Who: Huguenots, French-language printers. Era: 1740s to 1780. Status: gone (shop); present building at no. 296 not checked. Evidence: [Stadsarchief, 1747 Uitgeverij/boekhandel Rey-Bernard](https://www.amsterdam.nl/stadsarchief/themasites/amsterdam-migratiestad/1747-uitgeverij-boekhandel-rey-bernard/); [Wikipedia: Marc-Michel Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc-Michel_Rey) (lead, not opened). Caveats: the "printers who fled censorship" item of the brief; needs a look at what stands at NZV 296 now and whether the street number has stayed the same.

early-modern.name: Het Gekroonde Hof van Denemarken, the Scandinavian boarding house (gone)
early-modern.line: 19. **Het Gekroonde Hof van Denemarken, the Scandinavian boarding house (gone)** (Ridderstraat, between the Oude Schans and the Eerste dwarsstraat, now Nieuwe Ridderstraat; 1748 to 1793) (N): the Norwegian Rachel Theunis from Kristiansand, married in turn to two Norwegians, a Dane and a man from Szczecin, ran a cheap lodging house in the Lastage where migrant sailors from Germany and Scandinavia stayed; notarial records show her helping other newcomers. Who: Norwegians, Danes, Germans, Poles. Era: 1748 to 1793. Status: gone (street rebuilt). Evidence: [Stadsarchief, 1748 'Het Gekroonde Hof van Denemarken'](https://www.amsterdam.nl/stadsarchief/themasites/amsterdam-migratiestad/1748-'-gekroonde-hof-denemarken'/). Caveats: one authoritative source only (the archive itself), but it is a primary-record story; exact house unknown, place it on the street. Best "sailors' quarter" item for the slice.

guestworkers-and-new.name: Moskee Al Kabir, Weesperzijde 76
guestworkers-and-new.line: 4. **Moskee Al Kabir, Weesperzijde 76** (Weesperzijde 76; here since 1982) (N): Amsterdam's first Moroccan mosque, founded by guest workers in 1972-74 in the Van Ostadestraat basement (item 2), moved here in 1982 and still serves the community; it calls itself "a living monument of the Moroccan community". Who: Moroccans. Era: 1972 to now. Status: open. Evidence: Moslim Archief guide (D5/C5 "Weesperzijde 76, vorige locatie Van Ostadestraat 268"); canon window 41; mosque's own site https://moskeealkabir.nl/ . Caveats: could be a paragraph on item 2 instead of its own place; building history of no. 76 not checked.

guestworkers-and-new.name: Site of Pension Johnny
guestworkers-and-new.line: 8. **Site of Pension Johnny** (corner Amstelstraat / Paardenstraat; fire night of 4-5 Dec 1970) (N): an arson fire in a crowded boarding house for guest workers killed eight Moroccan residents and a Tanzanian visitor; there was one staircase and no fire escape, and four of the dead were not even registered. It exposed the pension trade and led to protests. Who: Moroccan guest workers. Era: 1970. Status: gone (building with the burnt floor stood until about 1976). Evidence: Ons Amsterdam "Brand in pension Johnny: één uitgang, geen brandtrap" https://onsamsterdam.nl/artikelen/brand-in-pension-johnny-een-uitgang-geen-brandtrap (read via BrowserOS, targeted); Amsterdam750 "Wanneer kwamen de eerste Marokkaanse arbeiders" https://amsterdam750.nl/verhaal/wanneer-kwamen-de-eerste-marokkaanse-arbeiders-naar-amsterdam/ ; de.wikipedia Amstelstraat (building until 1976). Caveats: nothing marks the spot; exact current building and number not checked. The best single place for the boarding-house story.

guestworkers-and-new.name: Moskee El Oumma
guestworkers-and-new.line: 14. **Moskee El Oumma** (Postjesweg 179A, Overtoomse Veld; built 1992) (N): Moroccan mosque paid for by a neighbourhood collection, described by UvA research as the first purpose-designed mosque in Amsterdam, beside the police station that came after the 1998 riot in the area. Who: Moroccan families of Nieuw-West. Era: 1992 to now. Status: open. Evidence: UvA press release 2026 https://www.uva.nl/en/content/news/press-releases/2026/03/purpose-built-mosques-tell-a-primarily-dutch-story.html ; Moslim Archief guide (A4, essay by Abdelkader Benali); mosque site https://eloumma.nl/contact/ . Caveats: "first purpose-built" is contested: the same city guide calls Taibah (1985) the first building built as a mosque; say "among the first".

guestworkers-and-new.name: El Hizjra, the first Arabic bookshop
guestworkers-and-new.line: 20. **El Hizjra, the first Arabic bookshop** (Frans Halsstraat 1985, then Singel 300 from 1992 to 2013) (N): Moroccan-born Abderazak Sbaiti and Simone IJben opened the first Arabic bookshop in the Netherlands; its foundation's writing prize launched Abdelkader Benali, Mustafa Stitou and Murat Isik. Who: Arabic-speaking (mainly Moroccan) migrants and their children. Era: 1985 to 2013. Status: gone (foundation continues). Evidence: Stadsarchief Migratiestad "1985 Arabische boekhandel El Hizjra" https://www.amsterdam.nl/stadsarchief/themasites/amsterdam-migratiestad/1985-arabische-boekhandel-el-hizjra/ (archive 1987-2013 at Stadsarchief). Caveats: no marker at Singel 300; current use not checked.

guestworkers-and-new.name: HTIB, the Turkish workers' association
guestworkers-and-new.line: 21. **HTIB, the Turkish workers' association** (Eerste Weteringplantsoen 2C; founded 7 June 1974 in Amsterdam) (N): left-wing association founded by Turkish workers and political refugees, still active; its women's sister HTKB (1975) was the first national Turkish women's group. Who: Turkish workers. Era: 1974 to now. Status: open. Evidence: nl.wikipedia Turkse Arbeidersvereniging https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkse_Arbeidersvereniging ; HTIB "50 jaar" https://htib.nl/htib-50-jaar/ ; IISG holds its archive (ARCH00589); Atria on HTKB https://atria.nl/en/kennis/artikelen/alles-over-de-turkse-vrouwenbeweging-in-nederland . Caveats: since when at this address unknown; office, not a sight; politically neutral wording needed.

guestworkers-and-new.name: Startblok Riekerhaven
guestworkers-and-new.line: 22. **Startblok Riekerhaven** (Riekerhaven, Nieuw-West; opened 1 July 2016) (N): 565 young people in temporary container blocks, half Dutch and half young refugees with status, an experiment in living together after the 2015 arrivals; copied at Startblok Elzenhagen in Noord. Who: young refugees (Syria, Eritrea and others) and Dutch youth. Era: 2016 to about 2027. Status: open (temporary). Evidence: gemeenteblad 2015 https://zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/gmb-2015-116797.pdf ; World Habitat https://world-habitat.org/?p=12702 ; NH Nieuws https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/311348/amsterdam-wil-andere-verdeling-jongeren-en-statushouders-in-grote-gemengd-wooncomplexen . Caveats: temporary permits (block 1 extended to 30 June 2027); residents only, view from outside.

guestworkers-and-new.name: Javastraat, a street of newcomers' shops
guestworkers-and-new.line: 31. **Javastraat, a street of newcomers' shops** (Javastraat, Indische Buurt) (N; only "101 Namen, railway viaduct" exists nearby): Turkish and Moroccan shops, the big Turkish coffeehouse Cinar Kardesler (run by Mustafa Cinar, who came in 1975), Turkish bakery Kapadokya, the Syrian-Lebanese grocer Tigris & Eufraat (2015) and Nadia Zerouali's Couscousbar (2017). Who: Turkish, Moroccan, Syrian. Era: 1970s to now. Status: open (changing). Evidence: Moslim Archief guide (C3/C4 Javastraat 20H and 30); Geheugen van Oost https://geheugenvanoost.amsterdam/page/93766/koffiehuis-cinar-kardesler-%C3%A9%C3%A9n-van-de-grootste-turkse-koffiehuizen-in . Caveats: a street, not a building; gentrifying fast; coffeehouse may have closed (interview 2011).

guestworkers-and-new.name: Imagine IC
guestworkers-and-new.line: 35. **Imagine IC** (Bijlmerplein 393; since 1999) (N): migrant-heritage archive-museum in the Bijlmer that began as a "Beeldverzamelgebouw" collecting first-generation migrants' life stories and images. Who: all migrant Amsterdammers. Era: 1999 to now. Status: open. Evidence: Stadsarchief Migratiestad "2004 andersAmsterdam bij Imagine IC" https://www.amsterdam.nl/stadsarchief/themasites/amsterdam-migratiestad/2004-andersamsterdam-imagine-ic/ ; Imagine IC https://imagineic.nl/over/bezoekersinfo-routebeschrijving/ . Caveats: institution in a library (shares the OBA Bijlmerplein); fine as a "where to learn more" stop.

guestworkers-and-new.name: Vluchtgarage, Kralenbeek 100
guestworkers-and-new.line: 36. **Vluchtgarage, Kralenbeek 100** (Kralenbeek 100, K-buurt, Zuidoost; 13 Dec 2013 to 13 April 2015) (N): office wing of a derelict parking garage where about 100 to 125 rejected asylum seekers lived for sixteen months before the court-ordered eviction. Who: undocumented refugees (We Are Here). Era: 2013-15. Status: gone or changed (city wanted it demolished; not verified). Evidence: Squat.net/Indymedia 13 Dec 2013 https://nl.squat.net/2013/12/13/amsterdam-vluchtelingen-we-are-here-naar-vluchtgarage/ ; rechtspraak.nl 2015 https://www.rechtspraak.nl/organisatie-en-contact/organisatie/gerechtshoven/gerechtshof-amsterdam/nieuws/2015/03/uitgeprocedeerde-asielzoekers-moeten-vluchtgarage-ontruimen ; NOS https://nos.nl/artikel/2013173-vluchtgarage-amsterdam-wordt-ontruimd . Caveats: NOS once placed it on the Karspeldreef; court gives Kralenbeek 100. Check what stands there now.

jewish-arrivals.name: Opekta at Singel 400, Otto Frank's refugee business
jewish-arrivals.line: 23. **Opekta at Singel 400, Otto Frank's refugee business** (Singel 400; 1934 to 1940) (N): Otto Frank set up the Dutch branch of a Frankfurt pectin firm in 1933 so the family could leave Germany. After a year in the Candida building on the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal it moved here, before Prinsengracht 263. Miep Gies started here. Who: German Jewish refugee entrepreneur. Era: 1933 to 1940. Status: changed (canal house, offices or shops; no plaque known). Evidence: [Anne Frank House research: Opekta, Singel](https://research.annefrank.org/en/locaties/5c893854-c6f4-4ec1-8bc7-3f53d91174cc), [Anne Frank House timeline: Otto starts Opekta](https://www.annefrank.org/en/timeline/30/otto-starts-opekta-in-the-netherlands/), [Wikipedia (en) Opekta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opekta). Caveats: could instead be a paragraph on the Anne Frank House (E: "Anne Frank House", n0ntsglbwukufqsfzdygtwcu), which would then carry the refugee-business story. Choose one.

jewish-arrivals.name: Comité voor Joodsche Vluchtelingen, Lijnbaansgracht 366
jewish-arrivals.line: 24. **Comité voor Joodsche Vluchtelingen, Lijnbaansgracht 366** (1939 to 1941) (N): the committee founded in 1933 to house, feed and place Jewish refugees. It first worked from 's-Gravenhekje 7 and moved here in 1939 when that building came down; after 1941 the Jewish Council used the address. Who: German and Austrian Jewish refugees, and the Amsterdam Jews who received them. Era: 1933 to 1941. Status: changed (present use not checked). Evidence: [Anne Frank House research: Committee for Jewish Refugees](https://research.annefrank.org/en/locaties/ee99471c-eda3-4963-a448-a980cb61c5f2/), [EHRI: CJV records](https://portal.ehri-project.eu/units/il-002798-6257542), [Wikipedia (en) Committee for Jewish Refugees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Committee_for_Jewish_Refugees_(Netherlands)). Caveats: the building's survival and look still need a street check (coordinates 52.360008, 4.894254, near the Vijzelgracht end). If it is gone, it becomes a paragraph elsewhere.

postwar-colonial.name: La Cubana, Max Woiski's club
postwar-colonial.line: 11. **La Cubana, Max Woiski's club** (Leidsestraat 52; 1942 to 1958) (N): the Surinamese singer Max Woiski Sr. opened his club in May 1942 and brought calypso and Caribbean music to the Leidseplein crowd, with a painted starry dome "as if on the Waterkant in Paramaribo" and his own brown beans and rice on busy nights; his son, who arrived on the quay in 1950, later ran La Tropicana. Who: Surinamese. Era: 1942 to 1958. Status: gone (building there; current use to check). Evidence: [Ons Amsterdam, Bruine bonen met rijst in de Leidsestraat](https://onsamsterdam.nl/artikelen/bruine-bonen-met-rijst-in-de-leidsestraat); [Parool, Max Woiski](https://www.parool.nl/kunst-media/max-woiski-van-de-muziek-naar-de-showbusiness~bfc9d91d/); [Data Amsterdam, Woiskistraat](https://data.amsterdam.nl/openbare-ruimten/0363300011952042). Caveats: opened in wartime; straddles the 1800-1945 slice (not on their list). Data Amsterdam says he played a club "in the thirties", Ons Amsterdam says opened 1942: use Ons Amsterdam's date.

postwar-colonial.name: Gunung Batu, the Moluccan Evangelical church
postwar-colonial.line: 12. **Gunung Batu, the Moluccan Evangelical church** (Jacques Perkstraat 1, Slotermeer; since 1993) (N): Amsterdam has no Moluccan neighbourhood, so the church is the community's fixed point; the Geredja Indjili Maluku congregation took over the 1960s New Apostolic church here in 1993. Who: Moluccans. Era: 1993 to now. Status: open. Evidence: [Gemeente Amsterdam, 75 jaar Molukse geschiedenis](https://www.amsterdam.nl/nieuws/achtergrond/75-jaar-molukse-geschiedenis/); [nl.wikipedia, Lijst van kerken in Amsterdam](https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lijst_van_kerken_in_Amsterdam); [Nederlands Dagblad, Amsterdamse kerk houdt Molukse cultuur levend](https://www.nd.nl/geloof/geloof/1167099/kerk-houdt-molukse-cultuur-levend-we-mogen-trots-zijn-op-onze). Caveats: the church's own Facebook marks 25 years "in March", consistent with 1993; build year of the church not yet found.

postwar-colonial.name: Tjalie Robinson's Slotermeer: Hugo Verriesthof
postwar-colonial.line: 13. **Tjalie Robinson's Slotermeer: Hugo Verriesthof** (Hugo Verriesthof 4; 1954 to 1962) (N): after Jakarta and two pensions, the Indo writer Tjalie Robinson (Jan Boon) settled in a still-unfinished Slotermeer street where many Indische repatriates were housed; he wrote about one coal stove for five rooms and the toko round the corner, and argued for keeping Indisch culture against the demand to assimilate. Who: Indische Nederlanders. Era: 1954 to 1962. Status: changed (ordinary housing). Evidence: [Stadsarchief, 1954 Van Jakarta naar Nieuw-West](https://www.amsterdam.nl/stadsarchief/themasites/amsterdam-migratiestad/1954-jakarta-nieuw-west/); [Ons Amsterdam, Indisch Amsterdam: Teruggekeerd (Lucassen)](https://onsamsterdam.nl/artikelen/indisch-amsterdam-teruggekeerd); [Indische Letteren via DBNL](https://www.dbnl.org/tekst/_ind004201301_01/_ind004201301_01.pdf) (gives no. 4). Caveats: no plaque known; a house-of-a-famous-newcomer item. Could become the Slotermeer anchor for "tens of thousands of repatriates in Nieuw-West".

postwar-colonial.name: Toko Ramee
postwar-colonial.line: 14. **Toko Ramee** (Ferdinand Bolstraat 74; August 1961) (N): Oen Poo Kwie and Oei Hwie Nio, a Chinese-Indonesian family whose relatives ran big restaurants on Java, opened this toko opposite the Albert Cuyp in 1961, naming it after her parents' shop in Salatiga; the grandmother of another family had run restaurant Djokja in the same street since 1954. Who: Chinese-Indonesians, Indische Nederlanders. Era: 1961 to now. Status: open. Evidence: [Chinese Indonesian Heritage Center, Van Toko Oen naar Toko Ramee](https://cihc.nl/foto-met-verhaal/74-van-toko-oen-naar-toko-ramee-deel-2-2/); [ONH, 'Toen die toko kwam...' (Amsterdam Museum Toko Mokum)](https://onh.nl/verhaal/toen-die-toko-kwam-was-ik-opgelucht-eindelijk-iets-indisch); [Amsterdam Museum, Toko Mokum](https://www.amsterdammuseum.nl/tentoonstelling/toko-mokum/9347). Caveats: new owner since 1998; Djokja is from a family blog (keasberry.com), weak.

postwar-colonial.name: Devi Dhaam Mandir
postwar-colonial.line: 18. **Devi Dhaam Mandir** (Grubbehoeve 32; at Egeldonk 1997 to 2010, now Grubbehoeve) (N): Surinamese Hindus in Zuidoost have never got the purpose-built temple they raised money for; their makeshift mandir by the flat Egeldonk was cleared for housing in 2010 ("our mandir is a house of prayer"), a new-build plan died in 2017, and the temple now meets in the honeycomb flat Grubbehoeve, next door to the Bijlmer Museum. Who: Surinamese Hindustani Hindus. Era: 1997 to now. Status: open (temporary space). Evidence: [Parool, Hindoes gaan morrend tempel Zuidoost uit](https://www.parool.nl/nieuws/hindoes-gaan-morrend-tempel-zuidoost-uit~bffb2f9d/); [AT5, Hindoetempel in de Bijlmer moet weg](https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/18612/hindoetempel-in-de-bijlmer-moet-weg); [AD, Zuidoost ziet bouw van hindoetempel niet meer zitten](https://www.ad.nl/amsterdam/zuidoost-ziet-bouw-van-hindoetempel-niet-meer-zitten~a89bb09a/); [Leiden dissertation 'Let us Live as Hindus'](https://scholarlypublications.universiteitleiden.nl/access/item%3A2856833/view); [Hindoeraad, Mandirs](https://hindoeraad.org/hindoe-gemeenschap/mandirs/). Caveats: current address from Hindoeraad only; confirm before pinning. A story of an absent temple: write it plainly.

postwar-colonial.name: Sama Sebo and De Posthoorn
postwar-colonial.line: 29. **Sama Sebo and De Posthoorn** (P.C. Hooftstraat 27 / Hobbemastraat; 1969) (N): the city's oldest surviving Indonesian restaurant, opened by Sebo Woldringh (conceived in the Indies, trained at the famous Restaurant Bali in the Leidsestraat, gone); the Moluccan couple Izaak and Rieka Wattimena came over from Bali as host and cook in 1971. Who: Indische Nederlanders, Moluccans. Era: 1969 to now. Status: open. Evidence: [Ons Amsterdam, Het huis dat Sebo bouwde](https://onsamsterdam.nl/artikelen/het-huis-dat-sebo-bouwde-vijftig-jaar-indonesisch-restaurant-sama-sebo); [Parool, Rieka Wattimena (1937-2018)](https://www.parool.nl/nieuws/rieka-wattimena-1937-2018-was-altijd-druk-in-de-keuken~b91f3ca8/); [Parool 2019](https://www.parool.nl/ps/gejuich-in-sama-sebo-want-ze-gaan-niets-veranderen~b185ac49/). Caveats: Ons Amsterdam spells Wattinema, Parool Wattimena: use Parool. Founder is Dutch-born: the arrival angle is the Indies kitchen and its Moluccan staff.

postwar-colonial.name: Warung Spang Makandra
postwar-colonial.line: 33. **Warung Spang Makandra** (Gerard Doustraat 39; 1978) (N): a Javanese-Surinamese warung, "strong together" in Sranan, in De Pijp since 1978, one of the few places that tells the Javanese chapter of Surinamese migration. Who: Javanese Surinamese. Era: 1978 to now. Status: open. Evidence: [Spang Makandra (official)](https://spangmakandra.nl/); [De Buik](https://www.debuik.nl/amsterdam/restaurant/warung-spang-makandra); [Volkshotel blog 2016](https://www.volkshotel.nl/en/blog/hotspots/londons-tip-warung-spang-makandra/). Caveats: weak (no authoritative source; Instagram gives Gerard Doustraat 33). Food round rule: worth visiting without eating? Marginal.
